podcast.title: 2010s Resurgence with Roots in 1950s/60s
podcast.body: While not a new genre of the 2010s, Indie Folk experienced a significant resurgence in that decade, with its foundational roots tracing back to the late 1950s or 1960s. "Then we have Indy Folk. It's not exactly a new genre from the 2010s. I mean, it's roots go back to the 60s or even the late 1950s, but it did have a new major coming out that decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: Alt Rock Fusion of Acoustic Genres
podcast.body: Indie Folk is described as a subgenre within alt rock where folk, blues, gospel, and even country music converge, emphasizing acoustic instrumentation, rootsiness, and authenticity. "This is a corner of alt rock where folk, blues, gospel, and even a little country came together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: Authenticity and Acoustic Vibe
podcast.body: A core aspect of Indie Folk is its emphasis on rootsiness and authenticity, typically featuring largely acoustic arrangements and cultivating a generally relaxed and quiet atmosphere. "An emphasis is placed on rootceness and authenticity. Everything could be largely acoustic, and the vibe generally relaxed and quiet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres
